title: Start with the related rectangle
text: A rectangle with base 10 and height 6 has area $$10 \times 6$$. The triangle is half of that, because the diagonal cuts the rectangle into two equal areas. A common mistake is to answer $$10 \times 6$$ and forget the $$\frac{1}{2}$$, or to add $$\frac{1}{2}$$ instead of multiplying. What is $$10 \times 6$$?

title: Worked solution
text: Area $$= \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 6 = 30$$. Common mistake: answering 60, or $$10 + 6 = 16$$. General rule: triangle area is $$\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$$. The height is perpendicular to the base, not the slanted side.
